# The Binding Band

Ten new items before you can have fun? It sounds like a lot, but they all follow one rule, and most of them land close to something you already build. This guide goes through all ten: what I designed it for, and where it fits next to what you already play. One assumption: you know the recipes on the main server by heart.

## Design & Motivation

With the introduction of BINDING_BAND, my goal was not to shy new players away and overcomplicate an already working system. We have to dig a little deeper into this. Once you understand the motivation and the reasoning behind why I designed and introduced the BINDING_BAND items, it will be much easier for you to learn the items.

Upfront, if you are a person that does not like to learn, I encourage you to change that mindset. It's good to step out of your comfort zone. Not just as a player about to learn the changes from PAC to JAC, but as a person in general. Being willing to learn and experience keeps your mind young and fresh. As you grow older, you should cherish any opportunity to broaden your horizon. It is okay to feel overwhelmed, but there is negative and positive confusion. Confusion is your body's response to things it is not familiar with. It's an initial state that will go away. You are learning. Don't be afraid to learn.

First of all, let's scope the effort. We have a new component, that makes 10 new items. That's it. Just 10 items. It's not that much. Compare it to learning a new language where you have to learn thousands of new words and grammatical concepts. Or learning a new game with completely new rules. This is nothing. All the BINDING_BAND designs I have thoughtfully crafted so they are easy and intuitive to learn. So what was the motivation in the first place?

If you have played PAC for a while and you know all the recipes by heart, you noticed every single stat in the game is represented, but one: LUCK. BINDING_BAND covers that lacking design space. LUCK itself affects all in-game stats related to chance. I assume you already understand the purpose of LUCK, because this is something that is an integral part of the main server. But as a repetition: anything related to chance. Chances in abilities, like Rhydon execute. Chances in synergies, like the chance to poison a Pokémon. Chances to proc certain effects, like the FAIRY wands.

The BINDING_BAND covers that exact stat which was missing! Every item you build with it takes one half of its effect from the band — the chance — and the other half from the component you add. For example, combine it with CHARCOAL and you get something chance-related and something attack-related. Easy!

Let’s go through each item and the reasoning behind its design.

## Everstone: Binding Band + Fossil Stone

If you ask me, this one makes the most sense. Alone from a gaming perspective. This game offers many synergies, some easier, some more complex. The most basic ones give ATK, such as FIRE; give PP, like WATER; AP, as in PSYCHIC; SPE_DEF, as in ICE; DEF, as in ROCK; and heal HP, such as GRASS. Foundational stats. Represented in foundational synergies. They give you more from what you already have.

All of them have a synergy stone, but ROCK. It makes a lot of sense that there are synergy stones that cover all those foundational stats. There we have it, a Synergystone that gives us access to the foundation DEF Synergy.

EVER_STONE stops you from evolving in the main game. The BINDING_BAND stands for something lasting and "binding". Well, and visually it makes super sense as well. It legit is just a stone. So there is our ROCK synergy stone.

## Soothe Bell

There is a chance (BINDING_BAND) that we heal (MIRACLE_SEED). This is how you would read the item just from its components. Well, it does exactly that. Another support option. Instead of giving you raw HP as a heal, I went with SHIELD. It's a more readable design, and it allows stacking as well. We see a small SHIELD bump on a low-life unit, and we're happy. Another sustain item, but more targeted.

Compare it to GREEN_ORB. Instead of a low amount to many units, it's a high amount to a singular unit. There is a chance it converts it to actual HP as well. This part is not really needed and was just added because it makes the experience more fun. Suddenly a unit becomes big. Gameplay-wise, it's not much of a change. The effective health on the board is the same. SHIELD and real HP are almost interchangeable. SHIELD is better against things like burn or poison that use max HP damage, but SHIELD can be skipped through flinch. So the conversion is less of a gameplay change and more of a visual-for-fun change.

But that is your support item called SOOTHE_BELL. Like all support items, it's not your first priority.

## EXP Charm

Win streak is strictly better than lose streak. Periodt.

Okay this is not true at all. If you care about getting 1st - both Win and Lose Streaking are exactly equally good. The extremes give you the most econ and swing the game the most. You lead, or you catch up. Though if you care about climbing — as in top 4 or better — win streaking is mostly better. When it comes to climbing, the game rewards you for playing the game, preserving HP and capping your board. So why are we talking about climbing and Elo? This is about design. I want to let people have another item that rewards them for losing. Something that helps you to catch up.

A unit holding an EXP_CHARM gives you 1 XP. That is 1 gold. If you build this in the early game, where you know your holder is going to get KO'd, you get the maximum value in terms of gold. The item itself has a chance (BINDING_BAND) to give you mana (MYSTIC_WATER). The numbers have been changed, tuned up and down many times in the past, to the point where it feels good now.

Some people might think this effect sounds broken. Others think it's too weak. I would say it's in the perfect spot where it serves two roles: it supports the losing side of things, while also, if paired with other items, providing you with a reliable effect. In this case, another option to generate mana. If you ask me, the best usage for this is on dashers. E.g. STAR_DUST + SOUL_DEW + EXP_CHARM on a dasher.

The name already tells you what the other part of the item does: EXP_CHARM. It's not using the official EXP_CHARM sprite, just so we don't confuse it with SHINY_CHARM. But it's already in the name: a mana-related item that gives us EXP as well.

If you ever thought, how can I "slippery-max" a Pokémon? That's your answer. If you think, I wanna lose streak from this spot, but still build an item? That's your answer.

## Fairy Feather

This game is all about dishing out damage or taking in damage. Me offense, you defense. Me defense, you offense. When it comes to damage, we have two major sources in the game: attacking and casting. It's simple. More ATK, better attack. More AP, better cast. More SPEED, faster attack. More mana, faster PP. Okay.

We have a chance (BINDING_BAND) to deal damage derived through DEF (HEART_SCALE). An item with FAIRY in its name, made from HEART_SCALE, is already pretty easy to derive.

If you are coming from PAC and are experienced with the game, there are other options to deal damage other than increasing ATK, AP, SPEED, or PP. The best example is POWER_LENS. It's good to have these kinds of options in the game. Being able to burn a component that is not offensive, but still increase one's DPS. Making defensiveness your offensiveness.

An item in exactly that category is FAIRY_FEATHER. It deals damage but scales off the holder's DEF. The item already comes with a lot of DEF. If you play on this server and would like to itemize a ranged, high-DEF carry, as in ROCK or GROUND, but you don't have any CHARCOAL, MAGNET, or BLACK_GLASSES, there is your answer. Make a FAIRY_FEATHER.

## Clear Amulet

We were just talking about being able to dish out offensive capabilities without relying on offensive components. This is another one of those: have a chance (BINDING_BAND) to defend against some sort of SPECIAL (NEVER_MELT_ICE). Okay, that design space is already taken by exactly POWER_LENS. So what else can we defend against? The answer is statuses.

CLEAR_AMULET clears you from any statuses and reflects those to ADJACENT enemies. Compare it to ABILITY_SHIELD: many units for a short duration. This is a single unit for a longer duration. It gives you 20 SPE_DEF as well. Damage reduction doesn't scale linearly. ASSAULT_VEST has double the SPE_DEF, but it does not defend twice as much. When it comes to armor, just small amounts have a lot of impact. The effectiveness decreases with higher numbers.

So there you have it. I am sure you had games where you needed SAFETY_GOGGLES or an ASSAULT_VEST in the late game, but you knew you couldn't build those items in the early game. It's too much of a commitment that early on and has no immediate effect that early. Build and make CLEAR_AMULET. It's the good all-rounder for tanks and bruisers. If you like slamming items without feeling punished, make CLEAR_AMULET. An amulet that clears.

## Destiny Knot

A support item made from a CHARCOAL. Nice. At this point you noticed I like support items. You are right. In German we would say we have offensive items "durchgespielt." That translates to "played through." Attack damage and casting sets are "played through." There is nothing more to design.

So that's why DESTINY_KNOT ended up being another design towards support. And a support item made out of a CHARCOAL is a very unique one, if you'd ask me. The use case might be very niche, but it is very direct and simple with this one: sac the unit, gain the buff.

If you ever were in a situation where you wished you could further buff your "hyper carry", there is your answer. Great in FIELD, LIGHT 5, MONSTER, or any ADC comps that have a very clear strongest ADC. You can make DESTINY_KNOT. It's on the same level as SMOKE_BALL in terms of support. You will gladly take this on carousels in the late game. You don't want to waste a CHARCOAL on this in the early game.

Some people do make it early. I have seen people use this to LUCK stack, but hey, they really know what they are doing, so let them cook. If you are like me and don't know what you're doing, again, think of it like SMOKE_BALL.

And if we break apart the words "DESTINY_KNOT," it does exactly that. Two Pokémon are destined to each other. The sacrificed unit shares its stats with the destined strongest unit. How poetic.

## Lucky Punch

Most of the designs so far, you can kind of derive the meaning from the name once you read them a few times. LUCKY_PUNCH is the easiest. If we have a Pokémon behind the target and we are lucky, we punch the items away from the target.

It's a good slam for people who enjoy playing positioning heavy synergies. It directly rewards people who can position well. The base SPEED of this item is 30. That is almost an XRAY_VISION. If you are an XRAY_VISION fan, think of it in terms of gameplay and raw stats like another core SPEED item.

A popular super-OG set is XRAY_VISION + RED_ORB + PUNCHING_GLOVE. You can replace XRAY_VISION with LUCKY_PUNCH here. It's the same.

## Grip Claw

If one item in this new set is both the easiest to understand and the most popular, it is GRIP_CLAW. This is just the scaling version of RAZOR_FANG.

The exact same itemization theory holds here, like UPGRADE and XRAY_VISION, or SOUL_DEW and CHOICE_SPECS. If you think you can scale up, take the scaling version. If you think you need immediate power, go with the immediate version.

## Covert Cloak

My favourite item. When I grew up, I read a fair share of fantasy books. When I read and think of a cloak, the first thing that comes to my mind are wizards and witches. In my head, magicians are beings that operate at range. So there you have it: another option in the game besides WIDE_LENS to make your Pokémon ranged.

We have a chance (BINDING_BAND) to increase AP (TWISTED_SPOON). 

Let's talk about gameplay. This item deals a small amount of SPECIAL to all Pokémon in range and synergizes incredibly well with POKEMONOMICON. Both items are visually very magician-coded. A magic spell book and the magic cloak. This combo is super easy to remember. Both items are made from TWISTED_SPOON.

If you come from PAC, you know AP in the early game is super weak, but super strong in the late game. You need the big casters to make use of the big AP. COVERT_CLOAK + POKEMONOMICON is an introductory course to learning AP comps. It provides consistent damage in the earlier stages of the game, independent of any synergy or Pokémon. The damage just comes from the items. You can play this on a Zubat without Synergies, and you would be fine lmao.

Only the best players in PAC understand how to play AP comps well. It's one of the hardest, if not the hardest, skill to learn in PAC. Many people reach the top without knowing how to play it properly. You don't need to, but this item will make it easier to learn it.

## Fluffy Tail

In the main game you can flee from fights. If we translate this to PAC, dodging is a sort of fleeing. Not really, but I am sure you know what I mean.

Also visually, if you combine two BINDING_BAND items—things that are visually "strings" — you get something built out of strings. Simple to understand, simple to learn. Not fancy, but it's good to have.

Gameplay-wise, I wanted to provide another option to defend without using the defensive components HEART_SCALE and NEVER_MELT_ICE. Dodging might be a bit cringe. But defense is defense. With this item, we broaden an effect that was previously exclusive to GHOST.

Think of it as an alternative to POKE_DOLL. You decrease damage by dodging. Simple and Clear.

So there you have it, my full take on BINDING_BAND. The philosphy and motivaiton why I introduced this Component to the game. Thank you for reading. Thank you for playing. Much love tegberen.
